title: California Approves $25B Homebuyer Loan Program, Targeting New Construction
summary: California voters have approved a $25 billion homebuyer financing initiative that could create new purchase mortgage opportunities for lenders and brokers, particularly those working with homebuilders.Proposition 37, which passed with more than 60% of the vote in the Nov. 3 election, authorizes the California Housing Finance Agency (CalHFA) to issue up to $25 billion in revenue bonds to fund fixed-rate second mortgages covering as much as 17% of the purchase price of qualifying newly constructed homes.

title: DSCR Lending Keeps Gaining Ground as Investor Purchases Slow
summary: Real estate investors are buying fewer homes than they did a year ago, yet debt service coverage ratio (DSCR) lending continues to gain ground in the market. A big part of the reason is that DSCR loans are purpose-built for property investors. Agency loans qualify borrowers on their personal debt-to-income (DTI) ratio, so every property already in an investor's portfolio can weigh on approval. DSCR loans qualify borrowers primarily on whether the property’s rental income covers its full monthly payment, including principal, interest, taxes, insurance, and any association dues. That makes them especially attractive to investors adding to their portfolios.

title: UWM Ties 40-Basis-Point Pricing Incentive to Broker Technology Use

Brokers must use at least one of three UWM services: Underwriting+, TRAC+, or Virtual Closing.

title: Even at 6%, Mortgage Rates May Not Be Enough to Unlock Home Sales

title: VA Lending Gains Market Share, but $41 Billion in Potential Volume Goes Untapped
summary: A new analysis from Veterans United Home Loans estimates that approximately 83,100 VA loans, representing $41 billion in potential mortgage volume, went untapped across U.S. metropolitan areas in 2025.The findings point to a gap between the number of veterans living in certain housing markets and the share of mortgage originations using VA financing. They also suggest that opportunities to expand VA lending extend well beyond the expensive coastal markets often associated with affordability challenges.
